fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes and told everyone the land was exceedingly good, that the LORD was with them, and not to rebel or be afraid (Numbers 14:6–9). The answer they got was a threat to stone them. I think that one stings. And right then, the glory of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 14:10).

Rejoice is a nice word, friend, but it's not the one the LORD uses. He asks how long they will refuse to believe in Him, despite all the signs He has performed among them (Numbers 14:11). Earlier that night the people had wept (Numbers 14:1). Rejoicing would have been a big change of mood. The word that fits is believe.

Yes, baker, that's true. The men who brought out the bad report were struck down by a plague before the LORD (Numbers 14:36–37). Two of the spies came through it: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh (Numbers 14:38). They were the same two who had spoken up for the land, saying it was exceedingly good (Numbers 14:6–7).

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.

Saying Joshua and Caleb had only said the land was exceedingly good leaves out their other words, including their call not to rebel or fear the people of the land (Numbers 14:8–9).

The claim that nobody in the camp is throwing a rejoicing party adds a detail the text does not give. The passage says the people wept that night, but does not describe everyone’s actions when the LORD speaks to Moses.
